Live Corridor Snapshot

Udaipur City (UDZ)

Main railway hub of Udaipur under North Western Railway. It serves as the corridor's starting point and is being redeveloped with upgraded passenger facilities.

Rana Pratap Nagar (RPZ)

An important Udaipur-area station developed to help decongest Udaipur City. It has passenger amenities and is part of the North Western Railway network.

Mavli Junction (MVJ)

A key junction in Udaipur district serving Mavli town. It has multiple platforms and is an important operational point on the corridor.

Fatehnagar (FAN)

A functioning North Western Railway station serving Fatehnagar, with passenger train services and an operational role on the Udaipur–Kapasan corridor.

Kapasan (KIN)

The corridor endpoint in this Saarthi view. Kapasan station serves the town and handles Passenger, Express and Superfast train halts.

How It Works

See how Saarthi transforms disconnected maintenance data into one coordinated, optimized railway block plan.

HOW IT WORKS
From raw defect data to a coordinated block, in four steps.
01

Detect

Pull maintenance defects and operational inputs from TMS, SMMS and TDMS.

02

Prioritize

Score each issue using safety, urgency and operational impact.

03

Optimize

Find the maintenance window with the least possible train disruption.

04

Coordinate

Merge compatible department activities into a single coordinated block.

One connected decision flow

Saarthi first collects defect and operational signals, then ranks the most important issues, calculates the safest and least disruptive maintenance window, and finally combines compatible Engineering, Signal & Telecom and Traction activities into one coordinated block plan. Tap any step above to view the complete flow chart and see where that step fits in the full process.

What this graph tells us: Defect load peaks at 15 in Week 3 and then gradually falls to 4 by Week 8. In this demo, the downward trend represents the effect of Saarthi identifying higher-priority issues earlier and helping departments coordinate maintenance blocks before defects accumulate.

What is being measured?

Total maintenance defects reported or detected during each weekly monitoring cycle on the Udaipur City–Kapasan corridor.

Why is it useful?

The trend helps supervisors identify abnormal weeks, track whether corrective maintenance is reducing the backlog, and plan resources for Engineering, S&T and TRD teams.

Saarthi — Complete Decision Flow

Tap a stage to understand its place in the complete maintenance-planning pipeline.

01

Detect

Collect defects, maintenance requests and operational inputs from TMS, SMMS and TDMS so disconnected information enters one planning pipeline.

02

Prioritize

Evaluate safety risk, urgency, asset condition and operational impact to decide which activities need attention first.

03

Optimize

Compare available corridor windows and select a maintenance opportunity that minimizes disruption to train movement.

04

Coordinate

Group compatible Engineering, Signal & Telecom and Traction activities into one coordinated block plan with a shared operational window.

Final output: a prioritized, optimized and coordinated maintenance block plan for the Udaipur City → Kapasan corridor.
